hook: What if you got paid for every G, T, A five sale?
open_loop: Frame 0 bubble 'HOW MUCH?!' plants how much per second; line 3 gives the per-second answer, and the biggest number (about $333 million by tomorrow) is held until line 6. Line 7 turns it into a spend-or-save dilemma.
payoff: One day of GTA 5's estimated sales is about $333 million.

lines.text: What if you got paid for *every *GTA *5 sale?
lines.say: What if you got paid for every G, T, A five sale?
lines.visual: Frame 0: Benny (money outfit) in a delivery cap holds a pizza box, smug; a big generic cash register with a gold '$ PER SECOND' counter at $0 and a wall clock sits beside him. Plain white outlined text 'GTA 5' (no logo). Bubble 'HOW MUCH?!' on 'every'. Snap-zoom on 'sale'.

lines.text: It sold *about *one *billion dollars in three days.
lines.say: It sold about one billion dollars in three days.
lines.visual: Badge 'ESTIMATED SALES'; stamp '3 DAYS'; counter climbs to $1 BILLION; Benny gasps, pizza box flies up; cash rains from the register.

lines.text: So you would get *almost *four thousand dollars every second.
lines.say: So you would get almost four thousand dollars every second.
lines.visual: Tick sfx each second; each tick the register fires a cash stack and a '+$3,858' badge; cash piles up and buries Benny to his eyes with a coin on his head; thud sfx; Benny shocked then happy.
Benny digs out, throws his cap, slams stamp 'QUIT' on the pizza box; hero pose, shades on, smug, flips a coin.

lines.say: Your friend asks for a loan.
lines.visual: The hooded stranger runs in, begs with bubble 'LOAN?!' and empty pockets (broke expression); Benny crosses his arms and shrugs, then slides him one coin; stranger slumps.

lines.text: By tomorrow, you would have *about *three *hundred *thirty *million dollars.
lines.say: By tomorrow, you would have about three hundred thirty million dollars.
lines.visual: Hard cut with flash; calendar flips one day; gold counter races up to $333,000,000 with 'ABOUT' and 'IN ONE DAY'; coin rain and confetti; Benny buried again, shocked, then laughing. Small badge 'NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE'.

lines.text: Spend it all, or *save it? Comment *A or *B.
lines.say: Spend it all, or save it? Comment A or B.
lines.visual: Benny points at viewer, thinking; list rows 'A: SPEND IT ALL' and 'B: SAVE IT'; stranger shrugs on the other side; gold headline 'COMMENT A OR B'. Hard cut after the last word (tail ~0.3 s).

facts_used.claim: GTA 5 sold over $1 billion in its first 3 days (retail sales estimate).

math_check: Python: $1,000,000,000 / 3 = $333,333,333 per day ('about three hundred thirty million'); / 86,400 = $3,858.02 per second ('almost four thousand', exact $3,858 on screen). Revenue (retail sales), not profit: wording is 'sold' / 'sales' plus an ESTIMATED SALES badge.
word_count_note: Counted on 'say' (G, T, A five = 4 words). Seven spoken lines; the video-generator should split into 8-10 scenes at word anchors (e.g. line 3 into 'ticks' and 'buried', line 6 into calendar flip and counter).
ip_notes: 'GTA 5' is plain topic text only. No Rockstar characters, logos, lettering, footage, art or music; register is a generic cartoon prop.

upload.title: What If You Got Paid for Every GTA 5 Sale?
upload.description:
Imagine every GTA 5 sale landing in your bank account. 💰
Would you spend it all, or save it? Comment A or B!
By sales estimates, GTA 5 sold over $1 billion in its first 3 days. That is about $3,858 every second, or about $333 million a day.
Not financial advice. Estimated retail sales (not profit). Source: Engadget, Shacknews.

changes_from_previous: (1) One premise, no switch: dropped the 'one second a day' rule, the $1.4M and $1M numbers, and the invented $10,000 car. (2) Narration is a story: quit your delivery job, friend asks for a loan; numbers only in lines 2, 3 and 6 (about one per two lines). (3) Biggest number last: about $333 million by tomorrow is the held payoff, after the per-second figure. (4) Plainer hook: 'What if you got paid for every G, T, A five sale?' (12 words). (5) Length cut from 73 to the count above (about 30 s at 2.1 words/s). (6) New foil: pizza delivery job instead of the lemonade stand (original, not echoing test #1). (7) Ending is a values split (spend it all vs save it), tied to the money in the payoff, instead of a lopsided math comparison. (8) Upload: removed 'gta 6 vs gta 5' and #gta6 (video does not mention GTA 6), added 'gta 5 money per second', kept 'Not financial advice.', description line 1 is a new hook.
